newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher, soars on gas, chill.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher, soars on gas, chill.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled sharply higher Monday, soaring on another rally in natural gas prices and forecast of very chilly temperatures in the western U.S. this week.
"It's going to be very, very cold here tomorrow," said a trader in Washington state.
Anticipation of a surge in heating demand pushed electricity and natural gas prices in much of the U.S. to new highs today, market sources said.
January natural gas deliveries at the San Juan/Blanco Hub finished today at $4.15-$4.25 per milllion British thermal units, up almost a dollar from Friday.

Natgas prices at major physical trading points mirrored rocketing prices in the futures market. NYMEX January Henry Hub gas futures settled up 61.6 cents at $4.467/mmBtu after postin an all-time record high of $4.560.
January electricity futures came close or briefly touched their own contract highs.
January California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up $1.81 a megawatt hour (MWh) at $27.31 after hitting a session high of $28.75, just of shy of its contract high of $28.85.
February COB finished at $1.47 at $20.97 after posting a high of $21.70. Other COB contracts ended 50 to 80 cents higher.
January Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up $2.95 at $28.55 after flirting with its contract high of $29.00.

February PV finished up $2.40 at $22.70 after posting a new contract high at $23.50. March PV ended up $1.90 at $20.50 after setting a new contract high at $21.60. Other PV months finished 40 to 75 cents higher.
Fundamental factors could support another run-up Tuesday, and any downturn would be dependent on natgas and physical power prices, some market sources said.
"I wouldn't see it drop down a lot tomorrow," said Houston trader said.
